situacoes.papel_tutor: A sceptical finance director of the student's company, who only accepts numbers and good answers to objections.
situacoes.descricao: The examiner is a sceptical finance director. The student makes the case for a proposal: their own, or this one: a six-month trial of a four-day week for the customer service team, with two extra staff costing 9 million kwanzas. Difficulty: the examiner raises two objections, one at a time (the cost now; the risk that clients complain), and asks once to approve the full year immediately, without a trial, which the student should refuse. Decision: approve or not, and on what condition. Discussion: Should employees have a say in how a company spends its money? Opposite view 1: managers are paid to decide and to take the risk. Opposite view 2: the people who do the work know best where money is wasted.

extras.frase_inicial: Now Part 3. I'm the finance director, and I'm not easy to convince. You have a proposal for me. Go ahead.

frases: That's a fair point. But consider this…

situacoes.papel_tutor: A board member of a chain of pharmacies, who prefers a different option and asks "what if" questions.
situacoes.descricao: The examiner is a board member of a chain of three pharmacies in Luanda, with 60 million kwanzas to grow. Options: open a fourth pharmacy in Huambo; a home-delivery service in Luanda; or a small health check service (blood pressure, diabetes) inside the existing pharmacies. The student presents the options with scenarios and recommends one. Difficulty: the examiner prefers another option and asks two "what if" questions, one at a time. Decision: agree on one option and one condition. Discussion: Is it better for a business to grow fast or slowly? Opposite view 1: if you grow slowly, a competitor takes the market. Opposite view 2: many companies fail because they grow faster than their cash.

extras.frase_inicial: Now Part 3. I'm on the board of a chain of three pharmacies in Luanda. We have sixty million kwanzas to grow, and three ideas: Huambo, home delivery, or health checks in our pharmacies. Which would you recommend?

frases: Were it not for…, … would be the obvious choice.

situacoes.papel_tutor: Two colleagues in conflict, Edson (IT) and Yara (events); the examiner plays both and always says the name before speaking.
situacoes.descricao: The examiner plays two colleagues and always says the name before each line. EDSON (IT) needs the big meeting room on Saturday for a system migration planned for two months. YARA (events) has booked it for a client launch on the same Saturday, confirmed last week. Each blames the other for not checking. Hidden interests: Edson cannot move the migration without stopping the company on a weekday; Yara cannot lose face with the client. Difficulty: YARA says once: Under no circumstances will I cancel my client. The student mediates: ground rules, both sides, interests, options. Decision: a concrete agreement. Discussion: Should a manager always try to avoid conflict in a team? Opposite view 1: conflict wastes time and energy. Opposite view 2: teams without conflict often hide problems.

extras.frase_inicial: Now Part 3. You're the manager of two colleagues who are arguing. I'll play both of them. EDSON: I booked that room for Saturday two months ago! YARA: And my client launch was confirmed last week. It's in the system!

frases: Before we start, a few ground rules…
So what I'm hearing from both of you is…
Correct me if I'm wrong, but…
What if…? How would you feel about…?

situacoes.papel_tutor: The owner of a small hotel in Benguela, who is not a numbers person and believes every rumour.
situacoes.descricao: The examiner owns a hotel in Benguela. The student explains the quarter: occupancy 62 percent (target 70, last year 58); revenue 210 million kwanzas; online bookings 45 percent of the total; guest rating 4.3 out of 5 from 120 reviews; a new resort is said to be opening nearby next year (unconfirmed). The student summarises, explains the gap and approximates honestly. Difficulty: the examiner treats the rumour as a fact (The resort opens in June, so we are finished) and asks once to promise 70 percent next quarter. Decision: one recommendation for next quarter. Discussion: Should a company share its results with all its staff, even when they are bad? Opposite view 1: bad results can make good people leave. Opposite view 2: people work better when they know the truth.

extras.frase_inicial: Now Part 3. I own a small hotel in Benguela, and you've looked at our figures for the quarter. Numbers aren't my thing. Tell me how we're doing.

frases: Looking at the figures, we can see…
…is said to be… That is not confirmed.
Based on these figures, I'd recommend…
